subject: Aurora Labs — Inference onboarding: SDK, auth, routing & policy next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora Labs discovery — SDK/auth/routing summary + proposed next steps

Hi Ben — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap of what we heard and a proposed set of next steps so your engineers can start validation this week.

Summary from call:
- Primary goal: put a low-latency inference pipeline in front of Aurora's customer-facing chat assistant with predictable cost.
- Key features: SDK-based integration, token-level cost visibility, embeddings for semantic search + reranker, and structured tool-calls for bookings.
- Constraints: data residency in us-west, strict key rotation and audit logging, procurement prefers a single SaaS contract for initial POC.

Technical points we discussed (high level):
1) SDK & Auth: we recommend service-account API keys scoped to inference-only permissions; support for short-lived tokens via your internal vault. We can also support OIDC for long-term deployments.
2) Routing & policies: suggest a latency-first route for chat traffic (p95 <= 200ms) with a cost-fallback chain that routes to an economical quantized variant outside business hours.
3) Embeddings & rerankers: index at 1536-dimension embeddings with periodic reindexing cadence; reranker as a second-pass model called via structured output to keep token cost bounded.
4) Tool calling: we can enable structured tool outputs and verifier hooks to ensure deterministic booking payloads.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf (pdf, 480KB) — quick steps for SDK install + sample auth patterns.

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA):
- Engineering validation: Dev Patel (I cc'd) will send an architecture sketch and minimal sample invoking the SDK (ETA: 2026-04-20).
- Security & compliance: Marissa will share SOC2 / data-residency controls and a template security questionnaire (ETA: 2026-04-21).
- Procurement: Ben to share PO timelines and any required contract redlines (ETA: 2026-04-23).

If that looks right, we can convert this into a short mutual action plan and share a DocuSign for the POC order.

Thanks — looking forward to the next call.

—

Thanks Stephanie — useful recap. A few clarifying questions for our infra / security folks so we can scope the POC: 

1) On auth: can Redwood support an ephemeral token flow where our backend requests a short-lived token from Redwood using a signed JWT (we prefer not to distribute long-lived API keys)?
2) On routing: how granular are the routing policies? Can we route by SLA class + region + prompt length (we have some long-context flows that can be pre-routed to higher-memory nodes)?
3) Embeddings throughput: what's the recommended batch size and per-embedding latency for the 1536-dim profile? We need to understand tail latencies for synchronous search use cases.

Happy to jump on a quick follow-up with Dev and your engineering team if that's easier. Procurement will likely want a copy of your SOC2 report and the initial SOW.

-Ben

Ben — quick answers inline and attaching the quickstart + a short architecture note.

1) Ephemeral tokens: yes, we support a signed-jwt -> exchange flow. You can mint a JWT on your side and call Redwood's token-exchange endpoint to receive a short-lived bearer token (default TTL 15m). We also support integrating with HashiCorp Vault for rotation.

2) Routing granularity: policies can be composed: region + SLA label + request classifier (e.g., prompt_length > 2000 => high-memory pool). You can express these in a JSON policy document or via our Console UI. We support fallback chains (example below):
- Route A (latency-first: p95 target 200ms) -> Model X (v1)
- Fallback: Model Y (quantized, lower-cost) if queue_time > 50ms or queue_length > 40
- Nightly routing: route non-urgent traffic to Model Z (cost-optimized)

3) Embeddings throughput: for 1536-dim models we typically recommend batch sizes of 64–128 for best GPU utilization. Synchronous single-batch latencies are usually 30–120ms depending on instance type and sequence length; we'll provide observed percentiles in the architecture note.

Ben/Stephanie — looping in a short architecture sketch and a sample policy JSON snippet below to accelerate validation.

Quick notes:
- Minimal SDK flow: server-side: (1) mint signed JWT -> (2) call /v1/token/exchange -> (3) use bearer token for /v1/chat.stream with streaming enabled. Client apps never see long-lived keys.

- Policy snippet (example):
```
{
  "rules": [
    {"when": "region == \"us-west\" && sla == \"gold\"", "route": "low_latency_pool"},
    {"when": "prompt_tokens > 2000", "route": "high_memory_pool"},
    {"fallback": ["quantized_variant","cpu_fallback"]}
  ]
}
```

- Reranker pattern: call a small embed + ANN search -> take top-20 -> run reranker (structured output) to produce a ranked list and confidence vector. We recommend limiting reranker max output tokens to 64 to keep cost predictable.

I've attached a tiny sample NodeJS snippet (inline in the SDK quickstart PDF) and an infra sketch (aurora_arch_sketch_v1.svg).

Action: I will post the minimal repo with the sample in a shared Drive link by EOD today.

—Dev
